articles.detail: 5 cycles, all 5 completed, avg 9 published/cycle — up from yesterday's 51

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active, no pause gate is set, and every goal metric cleared its target — skip-if-healthy applies. The one queued candidate (2026-05-08-numerical-density) edits scripts/write-prompt.md, which is outside the parameter set this audit may touch, so it stays queued.
weakestArea: Regional spread carries the thinnest margin. Five regions clears the target of four, but Asia fell 7 → 5 and Oceania was absent for a second consecutive day, while the Middle East (19) and the Americas (18) took 63% of the board between them. Science is the other soft spot at 9, its lowest of the week, down from 12 — sci+tech held at 34% only because tech absorbed the difference (9 → 11). Neither is a parameter fault: the selector's category floors were met and the feed simply supplied what it supplied, so this is a supply observation rather than a tuning target.
watching: Hormuz and the Red Sea produced blockade-arithmetic, escort-queue and thirty-five-hulls filings across separate cycles, with the corridor condition confirmed by only one side — worth tracking for source symmetry as the count rises.
Sudan's RSF designation coverage is aimed at the suppliers rather than the militia, and alongside Radio Dabanga and the famine-access reporting it reads as the opening of an IPC declaration fight.

Pakistan recurs through Swat militancy and the rally against it; Dawn was the corpus top outlet for two straight weekly snapshots, so the regional voice and the concentration risk are the same outlet.
Two 2026-08-12 eclipse articles are already filed ahead of date — check at publication that they are not restating each other.

Weekly multiSourceRatePct fell 24.3% (wk 07-19) → 19.2% (wk 07-26) even though today's daily count is a healthy 11; if the weekly figure stays below 20 it becomes the strongest candidate for the next experiment.
coverageGaps: Oceania filed nothing for the second day running — no Australia, no New Zealand, no Pacific island states.
The Americas bucket is almost entirely North American; a single InSight Crime filing carried Latin America.
Central Asia and the Caucasus reached readers only through TASS and NEWS.am, so the region arrives largely in Russian-aligned framing.
Science volume rests on a narrow base — Nature and Phys.org supply most of it, with the remainder coming from general outlets covering science incidentally.
context: A heavier day than yesterday (59 vs 51) with all five cycles completing and timing stable at 1068s (selector 288s, writer 287s, editor 96s). Spread quality held: 47 unique sources, zero duplicates, top source at 9%, multi-source at 11. No experiment has been active since the 2026-05-18 editor-effort entry was voided, and history says the obvious levers are tapped — selector multi-source floors were raised twice and reverted once, with the conclusion that the feed's ~9 multi-source stories per cycle cap the published rate near 22%, and the standalone cap is already trimmed to 22 for a freshness target now comfortably met. The next experiment should therefore target upstream feed composition (event clustering, or the regional source lists in fetch-news-api.js) rather than the selector. TOP_EVENTS_TO_FETCH stays at 8 — each unit is one NewsAPI token per cycle against a capped spend. Housekeeping: a stray content/articles/_check.py.bad plus several scripts/_tmp* scratch files sit untracked in the working tree; the build globs *.md so nothing is at risk, but they want cleaning up.
